title: Three-Dimensionally Printed Microfluidic Cross-flow System for Ultrafiltration/Nanofiltration Membrane Performance Testing
protocol: Design microfluidic device as two separate parts: a top part and bottom part.
Start making the bottom part by drawing a 40 mm by 60 mm rectangle using the rectangle tool.
Create a 6.2 mm diameter circle centered 10 mm from one corner of the rectangle using the circle tool.
Replicate the hole across the rectangle with 20 mm spacing for a total of 6 holes using the linear pattern tool.
Fillet the rectangles with a radius of 1 mm using the fillet tool.
Extrude the part 10 mm using the extrude tool.
In the center of the top face, create a rectangle 30 mm by 1 mm using the rectangle tool.
Cut 0.2 mm for the flow channel using the extrude cut tool.
Make a 1 mm diameter circle at the end of the flow channel using the circle tool.
Construct a path connecting the circle to the nearest 40 mm by 10 mm face, including a 4 mm radius made with the fillet tool.
Make a cut along this path using the swept cut tool.
Create a 3.9 mm diameter circle at the center of the flow path using the circle tool.
Cut 8 mm with the extrude cut tool to allow for fittings.
Repeat steps involving creating holes and cutting paths on the opposite side of the flow channel.
Create a permeate channel using the rectangle tool to make a 30 mm by 1 mm rectangle.
Cut through the channel 0.5 mm using the extrude cut tool.
Make a 1 mm circle centered in the permeate channel, 5 mm from an end.
Construct a path connecting the circle to one of the 1 cm by 6 cm faces using the line tool and fillet tool for a 4 mm radius.
Create a swept cut along the constructed path.
With the circle tool, create additional circles with a diameter of 3.9 mm centered on the permeate channel’s path.
Cut through these circles 8 mm using the extrude cut tool.
At the part's top 40 mm edges, use the rectangle tool to create rectangles measuring 40 mm by 5 mm and add 4 mm radii with the fillet tool.
Use the extrude tool to extrude 3 mm downward from these rectangles for handles.
Print parts using a multi-material photopolymer 3-D printer with a hard transparent polymer, including an overcoating of soft rubbery polymer on each part's face containing the channel.
Tap threads (M5) into feed, retentate and permeate orifices.
Use plumber’s tape to connect 1/8” fittings to the feed and retentate, and 1/16” fittings to the permeate.
Connect microfluidic devices to a pump, valves, pressure transducer, and backpressure regulator with 1/8” tubing.
Connect 0.45 μm filters to inlet tubes.
Discharge permeate to a flow-meter and beakers on balances via 1/16” tubing.
Attach continuous rotation servo to backpressure regulator with screws.
Attach standard servo to 3-way valve with tie-wire.
Connect servos and power supply to servo shield.
Connect pressure transducer, switches, and servo shield to microcontroller.
Connect microcontroller, balances, flow-meter, and pump to a PC for data logging and system control.
Configure balances to print data to their serial port.
Cut membranes to 40 mm x 8 mm.
Soak membranes in ultrapure water (3 x 10 min) with sonication.
Soak the membranes in 50/50 ultrapure water/ethanol for 1 hr.
Rinse the membranes with ultrapure water and store in ultrapure water at 4 °C.
Add 500 ml of ultrapure water to an Erlenmeyer flask.
Add 0.04 g of BSA and 0.29 g of NaCl to the Erlenmeyer flask.
Add 500 ml of ultrapure water to a separate Erlenmeyer flask.
Add 0.6 g of MgSO4 to the separate Erlenmeyer flask.
Add 500 ml of ultrapure water to a third Erlenmeyer flask.
Add 0.29 g of NaCl to the third Erlenmeyer flask.
Insert stir bars into each flask.
Place flasks on stir plates.
Mix solutions for 5 min at 500 rpm.
Configure the system for measuring a single membrane by closing valves to flow cells not connected to the flow-meter.
Insert one pump inlet tube into the ultrapure water reservoir.
Insert the other inlet tube into the MgSO4 solution.
Use a syringe to draw water through tubing to remove air bubbles.
Insert a nanofiltration membrane on the bottom part of the flow cell with the active side towards the feed channel, and place it on the top part of the flow cell.
Fasten nuts by hand and then tighten evenly with a wrench to minimize leakage.
Select ultrapure water with the reservoir selector switch.
Set pump flow rate to 2 ml/min and start the pump.
Adjust pressure regulator to 4 bar.
Set experimental parameters to switch reservoirs every 45 min starting with the water reservoir.
Set reservoir switch to auto, and start experiment.
At 60 min collect MgSO4 permeate in a tube for next 30 min.
At 91 min replace MgSO4 flask with flask containing BSA and NaCl solution.
Quickly stop pump and use syringe to draw BSA solution through inlet tube to remove leftover MgSO4.
Start pump again.
At 150 min collect BSA permeate in a tube for next 30 min.
After 225 min, shut down the system.
Remove nanofiltration membrane from the flow cell.
Flush out test solution inlet tube with ultrapure water using a syringe.
Rinse electrodes of the potentiostat test cell with ultrapure water.
Deposit 5 μl of MgSO4 solution onto the test cell electrodes.
Record resistance of the MgSO4 solution.
Repeat steps for depositing and recording resistance four more times.
Calculate the average value of recorded resistances.
Repeat steps for NaCl solution.
Repeat steps for BSA/NaCl solution.
Repeat steps for each permeate solution collected.
Calculate salt rejection using Equation 1: Ωs is the resistance of the test solution, Ωp is the resistance of the permeate.
Add 1 L of ultrapure water to a 4 L beaker.
Add 0.32 g of BSA to the beaker.
Insert stir bar into the beaker and place on a stir plate.
Mix for 5 min at 500 rpm.
Add additional 3 L of ultrapure water to the beaker.
Mix again for 5 min at 500 rpm.
Configure the system to measure 4 membranes in parallel by opening all valves to flow cells.
Place one pump inlet tube into the ultrapure water reservoir.
Place other inlet tube into the BSA solution.
Use a syringe to draw the water through the tubing.
Remove all air bubbles in the system with the syringe.
Insert ultrafiltration membranes on the bottom part of the flow cells with the active sides towards the feed channels.
Close the cells with the top halves of the microfluidic device and fasten nuts by hand, then tighten evenly with a wrench.
Select ultrapure water with reservoir switch.
Set pump flow rate to 8 ml/min and start the pump.
Adjust pressure regulator to 0.4 bar.
Monitor flux values of membranes with data acquisition software according to manufacturer’s protocol.
Adjust pressure regulator until average flux is 200 LMH ± 10%.
Replace individual membrane if flux is not 200 LMH ± 20%.
Enter experimental run parameters.
Select the ultrapure water reservoir for 60 min with a constant flux of 200 ± 20 LMH.
Select the BSA reservoir for 420 min with manual control of the pressure regulator.
Select the ultrapure water reservoir for 15 min with manual control of the pressure regulator to flush the system at the end of experiment.
Set reservoir switch to auto and start experiment.
Shut down the system after run completion.
Remove membranes from flow cells.
Flush pump inlet tube with ultrapure water using a syringe.
